clue.text: Dull cotton fabric doomed to failure

parts.note: dead can mean dull or flat, as in a dead colour
duck is a heavy cotton or linen canvas cloth

explanation.surface: A drab bit of cloth seems destined to flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead duck is an idiom for a plan or person with no hope of success.

clue.text: Expel lawyer from Pluto's Dive

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, another name for Pluto
a dive is a seedy bar

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown out of a nightspot called Pluto's Dive.
explanation.walkthrough: To disbar is to strike a barrister off; the capitalised 'Dive' looks like part of a club's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To disbar is to remove a barrister's right to practise, expelling them from the profession.

clue.text: A Liberal majority, practically

parts.note: most means the greater part, the majority

explanation.surface: The Liberals have nearly won an overall majority.
explanation.definitionFit: Practically and nearly are synonyms, both meaning very nearly but not quite.

clue.text: Deposit that should come off the bill, at the end?

definitions.text: Deposit that should come off the bill, at the end?

parts.words: Deposit that should come off the bill, at the end?
parts.note: the bill is a beak or nose, and the deposit is the drip hanging from its tip, not a sum taken off an invoice

explanation.definitionFit: Humorously, the drop of moisture on the end of a nose, as well as a bead of condensation.

clue.text: Highlights of the novel Sea Children

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The best moments of a novel about children of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but signals the anagram of SEA CHILDREN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lights hanging from the ceiling literally give highlights, a witty definition by example.

clue.text: Not accustomed to sun, due to come out

indicators.note: letters that come out differently are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone pale who never sees the sunshine is about to emerge into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come out' signals the anagram of SUN and DUE; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Unused to something means not accustomed to it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Japanese play, object of bagatelle

parts.note: No (or Noh) is classical Japanese masked drama
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: A Japanese drama seems to be about a game of bagatelle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a trifle, something of no importance.

clue.text: Cuts back on this in Rome blissful

indicators.note: back says the word for cuts is read in the other direction

parts.note: pares means trims or cuts
hic is Latin for this

explanation.surface: Someone is ecstatic about spending cuts in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for cuts; 'on' just sets the Latin word after it. 'Rome' points to Latin, not the city itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphic means angelic in calm, so blissfully serene.

clue.text: Turnover, it is emphasised, is one of these sweet courses

indicators.note: turning a word over means reading it backwards

parts.note: something emphasised is stressed

explanation.surface: An apple turnover, stressed as a point, counts as a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' looks like the pastry (which is indeed a dessert) but turns STRESSED backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Desserts are the sweet courses at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Several, eh? Rather!

parts.note: some means a few, an indefinite several
eh? and what? are both ways of asking someone to repeat themselves

explanation.surface: A clipped exchange: someone asks if there are several, and the reply is an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather!' looks like a hearty British exclamation of agreement, but the definition uses its other sense, 'to some degree'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather, meaning to a certain extent, is a synonym of moderately or fairly.

clue.text: Supplies shops

definitions.meaning: supplies kept in reserve, as in a ship's provisions
retail outlets where goods are sold

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both stocks of provisions and the retail premises that sell them.

clue.text: Carrying life cover? Beyond doubt

definitions.meaning: holding life assurance, the British term for life insurance

explanation.surface: Someone with a life insurance policy feels completely certain of the future.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain life insurance is traditionally called assurance, so a policyholder is insured in that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both certain and covered by an assurance policy, two separate senses.

clue.text: Short butcher's vague indication

definitions.meaning: butcher's hook is Cockney rhyming slang for look, so a short butcher's is a brief look
a faint hint or sign of something

explanation.surface: A meat seller gives a curt, hazy pointer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a butcher's' is British rhyming slang (butcher's hook = look); a short look is a brief sight of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief sight and a faint hint are both senses of the same noun.

clue.text: Eating pears ruined one's make-up in the Savoy, possibly

definitions.text: one's make-up in the Savoy, possibly

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Someone spoiled their make-up by eating pears at the Savoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' signals the anagram of EATING PEARS. The Savoy is a London theatre, so the make-up is stage make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasepaint is theatrical make-up, which an actor at the Savoy Theatre might wear.

clue.text: This noisy spirit gets politer with treatment

indicators.note: the letters given treatment are worked on and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A rowdy ghost improves its manners after some therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with treatment' signals the anagram of GETS POLITER.
explanation.definitionFit: A German-derived word for a ghost that makes noises and throws objects about.

clue.text: A fellow, articulate and wealthy

parts.note: fluent means articulate in speech

explanation.surface: A well-spoken man is also rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent is a direct synonym for rich or wealthy.

clue.text: Animal may make a fuss about ancient city

indicators.note: about says the fuss word is placed around the city

parts.note: create means make a fuss, as in kick up a row
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A beast might kick up a row over an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the fuss word around the ancient city; 'may' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature is any living being, especially an animal.

clue.text: 1, in grammar school, head individual?

parts.note: the top pupil at the head of a school class comes first
a person is an individual human being

explanation.surface: A head teacher at a grammar school counts as the number one individual.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' reads as the number, but here it is the pronoun I, which grammar classes call this form.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the pronoun I belongs to the speaker's own category, the first of the three persons.

clue.text: At that point, yonder, a trained leader

parts.note: yonder means over there

indicators.note: a leader is a first letter, here of trained

explanation.surface: Over there, a trained guide stops at that spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereat is an archaic word meaning at that place or at that point.

clue.text: One in casino changing capital

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word casino
changing the letters rearranges them into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gambler in a casino swaps currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I in CASINO, and 'changing' rearranges the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus, an example of a capital.

clue.text: Bring about change in musician's gallery

parts.note: MU is the Musicians' Union, the British trade union for musicians
the Tate is a group of London and regional art galleries

explanation.surface: Someone wants to transform the gallery where a musician plays.
explanation.walkthrough: MU, the Musicians' Union, is the musician's union; TATE is Britain's best-known gallery name.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate something is to alter or transform its form or nature.

clue.text: Country dance light in the prime of life?

parts.note: a hey (or hay) is a traditional English country dance figure
day means daylight

explanation.surface: A folk dance by daylight for someone in their prime.
explanation.definitionFit: A heyday is the period of greatest vigour, success or strength.

clue.text: Casual footwear for idlers

definitions.meaning: people who loaf about doing nothing

explanation.surface: Slip-on shoes for those who do no work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both slip-on shoes and people who laze about.

clue.text: Portrait of colourful old man, standing by river

parts.note: the Picts were ancient inhabitants of Scotland said to paint or tattoo their bodies
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A painting shows a vividly dressed elderly man beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing by' just places the pieces side by side. The URE is a Yorkshire river much used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painting or image of a person, an example of the broader word.

clue.text: Runs away from stumps

definitions.meaning: baffles, as a puzzle escapes one's understanding

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both evades capture and escapes understanding, so baffles.

clue.text: Emergency treatment to make tree steady

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree
staid means sober, settled and steady

explanation.surface: A first-aid idea: brace a wobbly tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names immediate help given to an injured person before a doctor arrives.

clue.text: Agreement to have free entertainment before the end of May

parts.note: a treat is something paid for by someone else, like a free outing

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here taken from May

explanation.surface: A deal lets someone enjoy a complimentary outing before May is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states, a synonym.

clue.text: Manoeuvring sheep abandoned outside

indicators.note: the first piece stands outside, around, the sheep word

parts.note: a stray is an abandoned animal, here used adjectivally
a teg is a sheep in its second year

explanation.surface: A flock is herded around a sheep that has been left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the abandoned word around the sheep; a teg, a sheep in its second year, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Strategy is artful planning and manoeuvring to gain an advantage.
